segments.chapter: Name, boyhood and early New Orleans
segments.title: Name change from Zeno to George Lewis, Storyville clubs and early New Orleans musicians
segments.summary: Lewis explains how he came to be called George and legally changed his name in the 1940s, then names the Storyville-area places he played and the older musicians he knew as a child, including Manuel Perez and segregation among bands.

segments.chapter: Learning clarinet and the Eureka band
segments.title: Bunk Johnson's Philadelphia concert band, why he took up clarinet, and learning
segments.summary: He recalls a photo of the band at the Academy of Music in Philadelphia, then talks about being drawn to music, a childhood violin, and playing funerals on clarinet.

segments.chapter: Learning clarinet and the Eureka band
segments.title: First E-flat clarinet and the Eureka Brass Band
segments.summary: Lewis describes his first time on E-flat clarinet in 1919, the Eureka band's organizers, leaders and trumpeters, and brass bands that did not play jazz.

segments.title: Older drumming styles, playing with Bunk Johnson, and arriving in New York
segments.summary: Discussion of older drummers' styles, his experience playing with Bunk Johnson, and his impressions of New York, its musicians and where the band stayed.

segments.title: How the music and the beat have changed
segments.summary: Lewis gives his view on how jazz has changed, repertoire, the beat in New Orleans, and the older drummers' overhead traps.
